extracted_claims.text: The original AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), as adopted in 2024, provided that obligations concerning high-risk AI systems would become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e. on 2 August 2026.
Multiple EU guidance and legal-analysis pages (pre-Omnibus or not yet updated) still state that the Annex III high-risk AI obligations 'become enforceable' or 'apply' on 2 August 2026.

The Digital/AI Omnibus Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) amended Article 113 of the AI Act to extend the application date for the Annex III high-risk AI system obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027.

For AI systems classified as high-risk because they are safety components or embedded in products covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation, the obligations were extended to apply from 2 August 2028.
The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on the AI Omnibus (Digital Package on Simplification) on 7 May 2026.
The AI Omnibus Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026, after being adopted (as a Commission proposal) on 19 November 2025.

The Commission's original Omnibus proposal suggested adjusting the timeline for high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months so that the rules would start to apply once the Commission confirmed that needed standards and tools were available, rather than on a fixed calendar date.

Commentators describe 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) as 'backstop' dates, implying the mechanism could in principle trigger earlier if standards/tools become available sooner, though the dates function as fixed deadlines in the adopted Omnibus text.

Article 111(2)/Article 113(3) of the amended AI Act provides that for high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III, the Regulation applies to their operators only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date, with providers/deployers of systems used by public authorities required to take necessary steps regardless.

The Implementation Timeline page (artificialintelligenceact.eu) lists 2 August 2026 as the date both for 'the remainder of the AI Act' (except Article 6(1)) and for the Article 113 operator transitional rule for high-risk systems already on the market.

The ai-act-law.eu summary of Article 113 states that Chapter III, Sections 1-3 (which include the Annex III high-risk classification and obligations), with the exception of Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027.

News/legal-analysis sources (Questa AI, AnnexOps, EU AI Compass) confirm that, following the Digital Omnibus entering into force on 27 July 2026, the current, binding application date for Annex III high-risk obligations is 2 December 2027.

Some commentary (RAIL, McKenna Consultants, CSA, Snowflake) published before or without accounting for the Omnibus's final adoption continued to treat 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations.

A 2024 Goodwin Law timeline and a Squire Patton Boggs chart, published shortly after the AI Act's original entry into force, project 'full compliance for high-risk AI systems' around 2027, based on the pre-Omnibus phased timeline.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations (high confidence). However, a Digital/AI Omnibus Regulation (2024/1689 amendment via Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence), pushed this date to 2 December 2027 (high confidence), with related product-safety ("Annex I") high-risk systems now subject to obligations from 2 August 2028 (high confidence). Many compliance guides and news sources have not yet been updated to reflect this change, creating significant confusion in publicly available material.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
The AI Act as adopted in 2024 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) specified that high-risk AI system obligations would apply 36 months after entry into force, landing on 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). This date has been widely repeated across EU guidance pages and legal-analysis sites not yet updated for later amendments (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment
The Digital/AI Omnibus Regulation (2026/1744) amended Article 113 of the AI Act to extend the Annex III high-risk obligations' application date from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). For AI systems classified as high-risk because they are safety components of, or embedded in, products covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation, the obligations were separately extended to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this Omnibus package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)), and the Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Commission's original proposal had suggested a flexible mechanism tying the timeline to confirmation that needed standards and compliance tools were available, rather than a fixed date, with flexibility of up to 16 months (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Transitional Rules for Existing Systems
For high-risk systems already placed on the market before the new application date, the Act's operator obligations apply only if the system undergoes significant design changes afterward, though providers/deployers of systems used by public authorities must act regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Post-Omnibus Confirmation
Multiple legal-analysis and news sources confirm that, following the Omnibus's entry into force, the binding application date for Annex III obligations is now 2 December 2027 (low confidence, due to source authority limitations) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists between sources still citing 2 August 2026 as operative (e.g., RAIL, McKenna Consultants, CSA, Snowflake — low confidence) and sources confirming the extension to 2 December 2027 (high/medium confidence). This likely reflects publication timing relative to the Omnibus's finalization.

A further discrepancy (not resolved by any source) exists regarding the Annex I product-embedded systems deadline: Snowflake cites 2 August 2027, while the majority of sources (AI Act Service Desk, Digital Strategy EU, AnnexOps) state 2 August 2028 — this one-year gap remains unexplained.

The legislative sequence described by one source — "adopted" 19 November 2025, political agreement 7 May 2026, entry into force 27 July 2026 — is internally ambiguous and not clarified across sources (flagged as low confidence/0.12–0.17 claims throughout).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are truly fixed in the final Omnibus text or retain a conditional "standards-ready" trigger mechanism as originally proposed. No source provides the full consolidated Article 113 text confirming exactly which sub-provisions retain which dates. It is also unclear whether ancillary milestones (e.g., Member State sandbox requirements) were shifted by the Omnibus or remain tied to the original 2026 date.

## Methodology Note
This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

source_links.notes: Every link points to a gathered source.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations (high confidence). However, a Digital/AI Omnibus Regulation (2024/1689 amendment via Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which entered into force on 27 July 2026, pushed this date to 2 December 2027, with related product-safety ("Annex I") high-risk systems now subject to obligations from 2 August 2028 (high confidence). Many compliance guides and news sources have not yet been updated to reflect this change, creating significant confusion in publicly available material.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
The AI Act as adopted in 2024 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) specified that high-risk AI system obligations would apply 36 months after entry into force, landing on 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). This date has been widely repeated across EU guidance pages and legal-analysis sites not yet updated for later amendments (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment
The Digital/AI Omnibus Regulation (2026/1744) amended Article 113 of the AI Act to extend the Annex III high-risk obligations' application date from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). For AI systems classified as high-risk because they are safety components of, or embedded in, products covered by Annex I Union harmonisation legislation, the obligations were separately extended to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this Omnibus package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)), and the Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy EU](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The Commission's original proposal had suggested a flexible mechanism tying the timeline to confirmation that needed standards and compliance tools were available, rather than a fixed date, with flexibility of up to 16 months (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Transitional Rules for Existing Systems
For high-risk systems already placed on the market before the new application date, the Act's operator obligations apply only if the system undergoes significant design changes afterward, though providers/deployers of systems used by public authorities must act regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Post-Omnibus Confirmation
Multiple legal-analysis and news sources confirm that, following the Omnibus's entry into force, the binding application date for Annex III obligations is now 2 December 2027 (low confidence, due to source authority limitations) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists between sources still citing 2 August 2026 as operative (e.g., RAIL, McKenna Consultants, CSA, Snowflake — low confidence) and sources confirming the extension to 2 December 2027 (high/medium confidence). This likely reflects publication timing relative to the Omnibus's finalization.

A further discrepancy (not resolved by any source) exists regarding the Annex I product-embedded systems deadline: Snowflake cites 2 August 2027, while the majority of sources (AI Act Service Desk, Digital Strategy EU, AnnexOps) state 2 August 2028 — this one-year gap remains unexplained.

The legislative sequence described by one source — "adopted" 19 November 2025, political agreement 7 May 2026, entry into force 27 July 2026 — is internally ambiguous and not clarified across sources (flagged as low confidence/0.12–0.17 claims throughout).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are truly fixed in the final Omnibus text or retain a conditional "standards-ready" trigger mechanism as originally proposed. No source provides the full consolidated Article 113 text confirming exactly which sub-provisions retain which dates. It is also unclear whether ancillary milestones (e.g., Member State sandbox requirements) were shifted by the Omnibus or remain tied to the original 2026 date.
